title: Ocean currents and climate
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:57Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is a Year 11 Geography card on atmospheric circulation that mentions ocean currents only in passing, so it is broader and at a different depth from a Year 10 Science point on how ocean currents carry heat and shape regional climates.

draft.title: Ocean currents and climate
card: An ocean current is a large flow of seawater that moves in a steady pattern. Some currents run near the surface and some run deep.
Surface currents are mainly driven by wind. Deep currents are driven by differences in water temperature and saltiness, which change how dense the water is. Cold, salty water is denser and sinks.
Currents carry heat around the globe. Warm water flows from the tropics towards the poles, and cold water flows back towards the equator.
This moves heat to places that would otherwise be cooler or warmer. Currents therefore shape the climate of nearby coasts, such as how warm or cool they are.
draft.remember: Currents move heat around Earth, so they help shape regional climates.

a.q: Which pair of things drives deep ocean currents?
opts: Differences in wave height and tide times
Differences in sea depth and fish numbers
Differences in cloud cover and rainfall
a.why: Temperature and saltiness change how dense seawater is, and denser water sinks and flows. Wind mainly drives surface currents, not deep ones.
a.clue: Both change how dense the water is.

b.q: A warm current flows along the coast of a town in the far south of a continent. How is it likely to affect the town's climate?
opts: It carries heat from warmer places, so the coast is milder
It carries heat to the town, so the coast is much colder
It adds saltiness to the air, so the coast is much drier
It stops wind reaching the coast, so the coast is calmer
b.why: A warm current brings heat from warmer waters, so nearby coasts are milder than places at the same distance from the equator without it. It does not cool the coast.
b.clue: Ask where the current's heat came from.

b.best: It carries heat from warmer places, so the coast is milder
